newsitem.title: INDIA: INTERVIEW-AT&T eyes Internet market in India.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-AT&T eyes Internet market in India.

text.p: U.S. communications giant AT&T is eyeing India as a big market for on-line and entertainment services linked to the Internet information highway, John Legere, AT&T president for Asia-Pacific, said on Thursday.
"Strategically, we are looking at the full range," Legere told Reuters in an interview.
He was speaking after a news conference in New Delhi to announce the launch next month of AT&T's mobile telephone network in western India.
"If you look at the full range of services that a customer wants, over time India is a market to which we hope to bring all the facilities that AT&T has," Legere said.
AT&T has already launched Internet-related services in Asia-Pacific countries such as Japan, Hong Kong and Australia.
Indonesia and southern China are expected to join the list soon, Legere said.
AT&T also provides services such as designing websites and setting up physical infrastructure for the Internet, he said.
AT&T was using the mobile telephone opportunity to build close links with Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd, India's state-run monopoly for overseas telecommunications, Legere said.
VSNL currently has a monopoly on Internet services in India but is expected to announce a policy to allow private service providers in coming months.
"As infrastructure grows, we can provide more business to our customers," Legere said.

While investment in the mobile telephone network with India's Aditya Birla group was a major one, AT&T's eyes were on a long-term future for both its global customers in India and Indian customers, Legere said.
India was expected to be among the top three markets for international long-distance calls by the year 2005, AT&T spokesman Virat Bhatia said during the interview.

"It is clear that with the population they have, as infrastructure grows, there is no way you can stop India and China from becoming the biggest markets," he said, referring to the two most populous nations of the world.
Both nations have opened up their economies over the past decade, offering big business opportunities.
Legere said AT&T's investment in the mobile telephone service project was the biggest in the field that the company has made outside the United States.
He said AT&T was using the project to study a much bigger Indian market. "Our learning on the Indian market has already been tremendous," he said.
